passage: Toddler room note, Friday. When Nikita's father collected her, Nikita waved bye-bye at me with her whole arm and said “Ba!” Earlier in the garden she had stopped, pointed a finger at an aeroplane and looked back at me, eyebrows up. I said, “Aeroplane! Up in the sky.” She pointed again and repeated “Aa-pane.” I will keep naming what she points at, and tell her father about this new word. 🙂 Gautam

qa.q: What did Nikita point at in the garden?
qa.a: An aeroplane in the sky.

qa.q: What did Nikita want when she pointed and looked back at Gautam?
qa.a: She probably wanted to share her interest and hear the name of the aeroplane. She might also just have been checking Gautam's face.

qa.q: What is Gautam's plan and why does it help?
qa.a: Gautam will keep naming what she points at, which teaches new words and shows that her gestures are heard.

qa.q: How might Nikita's father feel hearing about the new word?
qa.a: He may be proud and pleased, and try naming things with her at home too.

grounding: A toddler waves bye-bye and points to share interest, and the teacher responds by naming the object.

passage: Tejas, two, sat on his grandfather Hrithik's shoulders on the road to the bus stand. A buffalo stood by the roadside and Tejas pointed with a fat finger, looking down at Hrithik. “Bhains,” said Hrithik. “Big buffalo.” Tejas pointed again and said “Ba.” When the bus arrived and Hrithik's brother climbed on, Tejas waved his whole hand until the bus turned the corner.

qa.q: What did Tejas point at by the roadside?
qa.a: A buffalo.

qa.q: What might Tejas have wanted when he pointed and looked down?
qa.a: He probably wanted to share what he saw and get a name for it. He could also have been checking that Hrithik had noticed.

qa.q: What could Hrithik do next to help Tejas learn more?
qa.a: He could keep naming things Tejas points at and wait for him to try the words himself.

qa.q: What might the brother on the bus feel when Tejas waves?
qa.a: He may feel warmed by the wave and wave back, since the child is saying goodbye in his way.

grounding: A toddler waves bye-bye and points to share interest, and the adult responds by naming the object.

passage:
On the pavement outside their Johannesburg house, Jamal stopped and pointed his whole arm at a brown dog behind a gate. "Dah! Dah!" He looked up at Lindiwe, his gogo.
"Dog," Lindiwe said. "A big brown dog."
Jamal pointed again, then, as they walked on, turned back and opened and closed his hand at the dog. Bye-bye.

qa.q: What colour was the dog?
qa.a: Brown.

qa.q: What did Jamal want when he pointed and looked up at Lindiwe?
qa.a: He was curious about the dog and eager to share it with her, checking she had seen it too.

qa.q: What did Lindiwe do that helped Jamal's language?
qa.a: She named what he pointed at, "Dog. A big brown dog," giving him the word for his interest.

qa.q: How might Lindiwe feel when Jamal waves bye-bye to the dog?
qa.a: She probably feels amused and proud, seeing him use a gesture to say goodbye.

grounding: A toddler points to share interest and waves bye-bye, and his grandmother names the object.

passage: I'm Vishal. I drive the school van, and I see little Anand every morning when we pick up his sister. He stands at the gate with his mother and waves bye-bye with his whole arm, long after we've gone. Last week he pointed at the cows by the road and shouted something. His mother said, "Cows! Two cows!" He pointed again, then at me. I can't say what he meant. But I wave back every day.

qa.q: Whom does the school van pick up at Anand's house?
qa.a: Anand's sister.

qa.q: What might Anand's pointing at the cows and then at Vishal show?
qa.a: It shows interest and a wish to share what he sees; pointing at Vishal may mean he feels friendly toward the driver he waves to every day, though Vishal can't be sure.

qa.q: What did Anand's mother do that helps his early language?
qa.a: She named what he pointed at, "Cows! Two cows!", giving him words for his interest.

qa.q: How does Vishal see Anand's daily waving?
qa.a: Vishal seems to enjoy it and takes it as a small friendship, waving back every day.

grounding: A van driver sees a toddler wave bye-bye and point to share interest, while his mother names what he points at.

passage:
Sunday: Kiran pointed at the ceiling fan and grunted. Tanvir looked up. "Fan! Round and round."
Wednesday: on the balcony, Kiran pointed at a crow, then looked back at his father's face. "Crow," said Tanvir. "Caw, caw."
The following Sunday: the crow flew off the railing. Kiran pointed after it, then waved bye-bye and said, "Caw."

qa.q: What did Kiran point at on Sunday?
qa.a: The ceiling fan.

qa.q: Why did Kiran look back at his father after pointing at the crow?
qa.a: He was interested in the crow and wanted to share it, checking whether his father had seen it too.

qa.q: Which habit of Tanvir's helped Kiran most?
qa.a: Naming each thing Kiran pointed at, with a sound or word, so Kiran started using "Caw" himself.

qa.q: How might it feel for Tanvir when Kiran says "Caw"?
qa.a: He would likely feel delighted and proud, hearing his son use a word linked to the pointing.

grounding: Over a week a toddler's pointing and waving grow into shared meaning as his father names what he points at.

passage:
Joseph Uncle from the fourth floor stepped out of the lift in the Chennai apartment block. Karthik, on his Amma's hip, flapped his hand up and down.
“Bye-bye to you too!” laughed Joseph.
Then Karthik stretched out one finger at the window ledge and made a loud “Ah!”
Joseph bent to look. “Pigeon! That's a pigeon.”
Karthik kept pointing, looking from the bird to Joseph and back.
“Pigeon,” Joseph said again, slowly.

qa.q: Which floor does Joseph Uncle live on?
qa.a: He lives on the fourth floor.

qa.q: What did Karthik want when he pointed at the ledge and said "Ah!"?
qa.a: He wanted Joseph to look at the pigeon with him; he was interested and excited to share what he saw.

qa.q: What did Joseph do that helps Karthik's language?
qa.a: He looked where Karthik pointed and named the bird, "Pigeon," giving him the word for what he was sharing.

qa.q: How might Joseph feel when Karthik waves and points at him?
qa.a: He probably feels pleased and included, as Karthik chose him to share the moment with.

grounding: It illustrates a toddler waving bye-bye and pointing to share interest, with an adult naming the object he points at.
